headline: Sabres GM says Luukkonen will be ‘big part’ of team’s future as Hellebuyck trade rumors persist
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Sabres GM says Luukkonen will be a "big part" of the team's future even as Connor Hellebuyck trade rumors persist, noting that Luukkonen owns a .860 save percentage through seven games.

Buffalo's numbers back up the concern in net. Through nine games so far this season, the Sabres are 4-3-2 with 10 points, and they have controlled 51% of the expected goals, a measure of shot quality that gauges how well a team is really playing. That is roughly an even split, and at 5-on-5 it is a bit better at 53%. The problem is finishing and saving. Buffalo has scored 1.8 fewer goals than its chances would suggest, and its goaltending has been worse still: goals saved above expected, which compares the goals allowed with what an average goalie would give up on the same shots, sits at minus 5.4. That is the real gap in this team's results. The skaters are holding their own, so a goalie upgrade, whether Hellebuyck or a Luukkonen rebound, would matter more than any lineup change. It is still a small sample, and a .860 stretch can correct itself, which is probably why the GM is publicly staying patient.
